sec: Crystals in urine — figure panels · p747

items.q: Which panel of this figure page names its crystal but prints no shape descriptor at all?
items.exp: Panel F is captioned simply 'Cholesterol crystal', while every other caption carries a shape: rhomboid, bipyramidal/envelope, dumb bell, star shaped, coffin lid and hexagonal. (Book p747)

items.q: Match each figure letter with its printed caption — 1) D 2) E 3) F … A) Cholesterol crystal B) Calcium phosphate (in alkaline urine), star shaped C) Struvite (MgNH4PO4), coffin lid appearance D) Amoxicillin crystal, broom brush appearance
items.exp: The second row of photographs runs D — calcium phosphate in alkaline urine (star shaped), E — struvite (MgNH4PO4, coffin lid), F — cholesterol; the broom-brush amoxicillin panel sits in the bottom row. (Book p747)

items.q: Every crystal below is paired with the shape descriptor printed under its photograph EXCEPT:
items.exp: The coffin-lid appearance belongs to struvite; the cholesterol caption carries no shape at all. (Book p747)

items.q: Panels A, B and C form the top row of the figure and are captioned uric acid, calcium oxalate dihydrate and calcium oxalate monohydrate in that order.
opts: True — that is the sequence of the three captions
False — panel B is calcium oxalate monohydrate and C is dihydrate
False — panel A is captioned calcium phosphate
True — and all three are described as envelope shaped
items.exp: Top row: A uric acid (rhomboid), B calcium oxalate dihydrate (bipyramidal/envelope), C calcium oxalate monohydrate (dumb bell). (Book p747)
